question.text: What is a Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)?

answer.text: A statement showing only the holdings of one particular fund house
A consolidated statement showing transactions and holdings across all schemes of all mutual funds for a common PAN
A bank account statement showing SIP deductions
A tax computation statement from the Income Tax department

explanation.text: The Logic: CAS (Consolidated Account Statement) is a single statement that shows transactions and holdings across all schemes of all mutual funds for a common PAN. It is generated by the RTAs (CAMS and KFintech) and sent to the investor based on the PAN linkage of folios. The Trap: CAS covers all mutual fund holdings linked to a PAN, not just one fund house. Monthly CAS is sent only when there are transactions in that month, while a half-yearly CAS is sent to all investors with folios linked to a PAN even if there are no transactions. Note: Investors can also access folio details across fund houses through MFCentral and the CAMS/KFintech websites; CAS itself is the standardised PAN-based statement defined in the workbook.
